$comment: ELF64 relocatable + dynamic for AArch64 (Linux / SysV). Ships at the D-LK6-1 sibling cycle (2026-06-01) — the closed-enum RelocFormulaKind reshape unblocked ARM64 reloc formula application. Consumed by `src/link/format/elf.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Section names + flags + ELF identity fields are the SAME values readelf prints; relocation `nativeId` values are the ELF type numbers stored in `r_info` low 32 bits (per the AArch64 ELF ABI, https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa).
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: ELF has NO image field for a stack SIZE on ANY flavor -- PT_GNU_STACK encodes stack EXECUTABILITY, not size. The kernel sizes the initial thread's stack from the process limit (`ulimit -s` / setrlimit RLIMIT_STACK) and further threads from pthread_attr_setstacksize, so nothing the linker writes can change it. A `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is therefore REFUSED with that remedy rather than silently dropped -- which is also why the sqlite full tier passes on Linux (8 MiB by default) and overflowed on Windows at 1 MiB.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c-subset long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Linux/POSIX header names are matched BYTE-EXACT -- `#include <Stdio.h>` does NOT name `stdio.h`, and a conforming toolchain must reject it. REQUIRED closed-enum field: the loader rejects a missing or unknown value. DSS performs the comparison ITSELF (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) rather than calling fs::exists and inheriting the BUILD HOST's convention -- without that, an elf target built on Windows/macOS silently ACCEPTED `<Stdio.h>` and emitted a real object (MEASURED 2026-08-04).
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: System V / ELF applies NO decoration to a C identifier -- the linker-visible name IS the identifier. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`nm -D /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6`, WSL Ubuntu): glibc exports `exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5`, `printf@@GLIBC_2.2.5` and `fstat64@@GLIBC_2.33` under exactly their C spellings. THE SAME COMMAND IS ALSO WHY `none` IS A POSITIVE ANSWER AND NOT AN ABSENCE: `_exit@@GLIBC_2.2.5` is exported TOO and is a DIFFERENT FUNCTION -- POSIX `_exit(2)`, which does NOT flush stdio -- so a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would not merely produce an ugly name, it would silently bind every `exit` to the non-flushing wrapper and lose buffered output. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c-subset/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: Linux arm64 (AAPCS64) uses the generic LSB-first bit-field allocation — identical to SysV/GNU gnu_packed for little-endian — so it shares the strategy. Byte-ABI-exact (the qemu arm64-ELF corpus is self-consistent under it; the CI cross-compile-compare confirms against the native compiler).
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: AAPCS64 linux-arm64 `long double` = IEEE binary128, 16/16. See elf64-aarch64-linux-exec.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE + D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (c145): a relocatable object carries data — a global lands in `.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss`/`.data.rel.ro` with `sh_addr=0` + a section-relative `.symtab` entry the FINAL linker binds. Same machine-NEUTRAL elf.cpp ET_REL writer as elf64-x86_64-linux (it reads section names/flags + reloc nativeIds from THIS schema, never hardcoding a machine); arch differs only via config — the abs64 data reloc is R_AARCH64_ABS64 (257) here vs R_X86_64_64 (1) on x86_64. A reloc-bearing CONST global (`relro`) emits `.rela.data.rel.ro`; a reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer emits `.rela.data`. TLS (`tdata`/`tbss`) is deferred to a follow-up.
$externCallDispatchComment: D-LK-ARM64-ELF-RELOC-EXTERN-DISPATCH (mirrors x86_64's D-LK-OBJECT-EXTERN-CALL-RELOCATABLE c141): extern FUNCTION calls in a RELOCATABLE object lower to a PLAIN DIRECT `BL` + a branch relocation against the UNDEFINED extern symbol — the SAME call-site shape as the arm64 exec `direct-plt`, except the FINAL (foreign) linker synthesizes the PLT/veneer and resolves the symbol, not DSS. So `direct-plt` is the right dispatch here too; the machine-NEUTRAL elf.cpp ET_REL writer emits the extern as an SHN_UNDEF `.symtab` entry + a `.rela.text` reloc rather than a DSS-synthesized stub. The undefined-extern CALL reloc is R_AARCH64_CALL26 (283) — and, UNLIKE x86_64 (which needs the PC32→PLT32 `pltNativeId` swap so a foreign `-pie` link routes through a linker PLT), AArch64 has NO distinct PLT-variant branch reloc: `R_AARCH64_CALL26` against an undefined symbol is exactly what gcc/clang emit for `bl printf` in a `.o`, and the linker inserts the veneer/PLT transparently. So the CALL26 reloc row deliberately carries NO `pltNativeId` (the writer emits its plain `nativeId` 283). The arm64 EXEC + macho-arm64-relocatable formats prove this `direct-plt`+CALL26-without-pltNativeId shape.
$externAddrBindingComment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): taking the ADDRESS of an undefined/preemptible extern (function OR data) as a LIVE code-form VALUE -- an argument, an automatic's initializer, a returned function pointer (NOT a call, NOT a static-data-item initializer) -- must materialize THROUGH a GOT slot the FINAL (foreign) linker synthesizes: arm64 `adrp x,:got:sym` (R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE) + `ldr x,[x,:got_lo12:sym]` (R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC). This relocatable `.o` is linked by a foreign DEFAULT-PIE toolchain (aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc with no -no-pie); an ABSOLUTE `adrp`+`add` (ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 + ADD_ABS_LO12_NC) against a symbol that may bind externally is REJECTED ('relocation R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 against symbol ... which may bind externally can not be used when making a shared object'). sqlite3.c -> arm64 .o has 3 such residuals (dlsym / sqlite3_search_count / stdout). The GOT indirection is exactly what gcc/clang emit for `&extern` in a default-PIE `.o`. DSS-NEUTRAL to x86_64 (its `&extern` value is a PC-relative rel32, already PIE-safe) and to the DSS-linked arm64 EXEC (it uses `dataImportBinding: copy-relocation` for data + a direct address for functions) and to the arm64 PIE/dyn formats (the c117 DSS-local __got slot) -- so ONLY the relocatable + static-archive formats declare it. Consumed by MIR->LIR `lowerGlobalAddr`'s value-form arm (keyed on the capability-derived symbol set, never a format/arch identity branch).

elf.$comment: Elf64_Ehdr identity fields. `class` = ELFCLASS64; `data` = ELFDATA2LSB (little-endian — AArch64 is little-endian by convention on Linux); `osabi` = ELFOSABI_NONE (SysV); `machine` = EM_AARCH64 (183).

sections.$comment: Executable code. sh_type = SHT_PROGBITS (1); sh_flags = SHF_ALLOC | SHF_EXECINSTR (0x6); addralign = 16 (cache-friendly; ARM64 instructions are 4-byte but section alignment is conventionally larger).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Relocation table for .text. sh_type = SHT_RELA (4); sh_flags = SHF_INFO_LINK (0x40); addralign = 8; entrysize = 24 (Elf64_Rela). sh_link/sh_info set per-link.
sections.name: .rela.text

sections.$comment: Symbol table. sh_type = SHT_SYMTAB (2); addralign = 8; entrysize = 24 (Elf64_Sym).
sections.name: .symtab

sections.$comment: Symbol-name string table. sh_type = SHT_STRTAB (3); addralign = 1.
sections.name: .strtab

sections.$comment: Section-header string table. sh_type = SHT_STRTAB (3); addralign = 1.
sections.name: .shstrtab

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-EXTERN-SYMBOL-NAMES: empty non-executable-stack marker for foreign-toolchain interop. sh_type = SHT_PROGBITS (1); sh_flags = 0 (NO SHF_EXECINSTR); addralign = 1; size 0. The ELF writer emits it (appended last, ET_REL only) iff this row is present.
sections.name: .note.GNU-stack

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE: read-only initialized data (string literals, const globals). SHT_PROGBITS(1); SHF_ALLOC(2). sh_addr=0 in a relocatable object — the final linker assigns the VA. Same machine-neutral writer as x86_64.
sections.name: .rodata

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE: writable initialized data (mutable globals). SHT_PROGBITS(1); SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3). sh_addr=0 in a relocatable object.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE: zero-initialized data (tentative globals `int g;`). SHT_NOBITS(8) — occupies no file bytes. SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3). sh_addr=0 in a relocatable object.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (c145): relocated-read-only const data — a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;`). gcc's `.data.rel.ro` contract: SHT_PROGBITS(1) + SHF_ALLOC|SHF_WRITE(3) (the loader writes the resolved target VA into each slot; a foreign linker places it in GNU_RELRO, read-only after relocation). sh_addr=0 in a relocatable object. The writer emits this section's OWN relocations into `.rela.data.rel.ro` (R_AARCH64_ABS64, abs64) — the `.rela.<section>` name is synthesized from this row's name.
sections.name: .data.rel.ro

relocations.$comment: 26-bit PC-relative branch with link / branch (BL / B target). ELF type R_AARCH64_CALL26 = 283. `kind` = 1 matches arm64.target.json's `call26` row.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_CALL26

relocations.$comment: 21-bit PC-relative page-pair (ADRP). ELF type R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 = 275. `kind` = 2 matches arm64.target.json's `adr_prel_pg_hi21` row.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21

relocations.$comment: 12-bit absolute low (ADD imm12 / LDST imm12). ELF type R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC = 277. `kind` = 3 matches arm64.target.json's `add_abs_lo12_nc` row.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC

relocations.$comment: Absolute 64-bit (data pointer). ELF type R_AARCH64_ABS64 = 257. `kind` = 4 matches arm64.target.json's `abs64` row.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ABS64

relocations.$comment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): GOT-entry page (ADRP of `:got:sym`). ELF type R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE = 311. `kind` = 7 matches arm64.target.json's `adr_got_page` row (the ADRP word of the `lea_extern_got` macro). Emitted only into this relocatable object; the foreign linker synthesizes the GOT slot + patches the ADRP page-delta. DSS never applies it (the exec_reloc_apply kernel arm fail-loud-refuses).
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE

relocations.$comment: D-LK-ARM64-EXTERN-DATA-ADDR-PIE-GOT (TF-C52): GOT-entry low-12 scaled offset (LDR of `[x,:got_lo12:sym]`). ELF type R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC = 312. `kind` = 8 matches arm64.target.json's `ld64_got_lo12` row (the LDR word of the `lea_extern_got` macro). Paired with R_AARCH64_ADR_GOT_PAGE against the same symbol; the foreign linker patches the scaled GOT-slot offset.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_LD64_GOT_LO12_NC

relocations.$comment: D-UNWIND-NO-EH-FRAME-IN-RELOCATABLE-OBJECTS: the DWARF FDE `initial_location` pointer in a relocatable `.eh_frame` (DW_EH_PE_pcrel|sdata4). ELF type R_AARCH64_PREL32 = 261 -- a 32-bit PC-relative DATA word, the only aarch64 row here that patches data rather than an instruction field. `kind` = 9 matches arm64.target.json's `pcrel32` row. No `pltNativeId`: an FDE pointer never names an extern call. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 against `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc -c`: `readelf -r` shows `R_AARCH64_PREL32  .text + <fnOffset>` on every FDE -- the reference toolchain's own choice, not an inference.
relocations.name: R_AARCH64_PREL32
